(1) the access device resistance is the dominant factor for determining the heating profile of the phase-change element and the resulting amorphization, and (2) the access device must be designed to minimize wasted power and to maximize reset speed.
the reset of phase-change memory elements depends on the load and pulse rise time, with the latter being the more critical parameter.

(i) the heating of the phase-change material (PCM) is a non-linear function of the applied voltage, (ii) the amorphization profile in the PCM depends on the pulse rise time and (iii) the amorphized region is a function of the applied current density.

the development of a detailed physical model of phase-change memory (PCM) cells and their operation.
the physics of phase-change memory (PCM) cells and their access devices.
the physical modeling of the reset operation in PCM cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the access device and its load play an important role in the reset operation, and the pulse width and load are important parameters for the reset operation.

the operation dynamics of the reset operation of the phase-change memory cells are very sensitive to the loads and pulse rise-times applied, and that the operation dynamics can be controlled by adjusting the access devices (and the cell design).

the access devices play a crucial role for the reset operation in phase-change memory cells, and that a detailed physical model of heating and amorphification is necessary in order to optimize the programming conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination of the following factors are necessary for a robust reset operation: (a) A high enough load to overcome the resistance of the phase-change material, (b) a low enough rise time to allow the heat to be conducted to the phase-change material before the pulse is turned off, and (c) a high enough temperature to melt the material, but not so high that a lot of power is wasted.
a detailed understanding of the physical operation of phase-change memories, including the role of access devices, is required for the optimization of the memory cell operation.

the access devices can have a strong impact on the dynamics of the phase-change process, and the results are very different for different access device types.

the programming of phase-change memory is not only a matter of the phase change material, but also of the access devices and the programming scheme, and that the latter can be optimized to achieve a better trade-off between programming speed, power consumption, and endurance.
